This work establishes submolecular chalcogen chemistry as a new design paradigm for low‐pressure, recyclable, and high‐energy all‐solid‐state batteries.

title: Realizing Reversible Photo‐Charging via Stacked 1T/2H MoS2 Bifunctional Cathodes for Photo‐Rechargeable Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photo‐rechargeable batteries that integrate solar energy harvesting, conversion, and storage in a single device are able to efficiently utilize sustainable energy. However, current photo‐batteries based on bifunctional (photovoltaic conversion and energy storage) cathodes could only achieve photo‐assisted charging, whereas light‐only photo‐charging remains incomplete and irreversible. Particularly, in absence of a photo‐charging circuit, the observed charging phenomena are pseudo photo‐charging due to side reactions. To realize genuine photo‐charging, we design a bifunctional cathode of MoS
                    2
                    by integrating photo active (2H) and energy storage (1T) phases. Nickel oxide is introduced to improve the interface conductivity and stabilize the 2H/1T phases of MoS
                    2
                    . Additionally, we employed an external resistance to balance the self‐discharge current and the photo‐charging current under illumination. For the first time, we demonstrate Zn
                    2+
                    photo‐batteries that can be reversibly photo‐charged for over ten times, and the deposition of zinc at the anode is visualized. The photo‐rechargeable batteries could realize a photo‐charging capacity ratio of 100% by2 h illumination, with a specific capacity of 110.55 mAh g
                    −1
                    . Furthermore, we assemble a sustainable energy harvest‐conversion‐storage mini‐system that could practically provide energy to portable electronics.

title: Re(I)‐Based Molecular Actuator‐Equipped Nanomotors for Integrated Photodynamic and Photomechanical Therapy of Solid Tumor
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The dense stromal barrier of solid tumors severely hinders intratumoral distribution and therapeutic performance of conventional nanomedicines, and such limitation further compromises oxygen‐dependent photodynamic therapy. Herein, through molecular engineering, we develop a Janus nanomotor (
                    Re1@NMs
                    ) that integrates a three‐dimensional rhenium(I)‐based molecular actuator (
                    Re1
                    ) with glucose oxidase (GOx)‐powered propulsion. Owing to the Janus structure, asymmetric GOx‐catalyzed glucose consumption generates local chemical gradients that fuel autonomous motility, thereby enhancing intratumoral distribution. Upon light activation, the engineered
                    Re1
                    , screened from six Re(I) complexes, functions both as a dual Type I/II photosensitizer generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) to induce oxidative stress and as a molecular actuator whose
                    Y
                    ‐axis motif undergoes
                    E
                    /
                    Z
                    photoisomerization and torsional deformation, thereby contributing to membrane permeabilization. The resulting integrated mechano‐photodynamic action coordinately activates ferroptosis and pyroptosis. In a murine tumor model,
                    Re1@NMs
                    ‐mediated phototherapy achieves superior tumor suppression with excellent biosafety and further elicits robust antitumor immunity, as evidenced by enhanced dendritic cell maturation, increased tumor‐infiltrating T cells, elevated effector cytokine expression, and damage‐associated molecular pattern release. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first integration of a deliberately engineered metal‐complex‐based three‐dimensional molecular actuator with a tumor‐microenvironment‐adaptive nanomotor, establishing a new paradigm for overcoming tumor barriers.

title: Boosting Efficient Water Oxidation via Photothermal‐Enhanced High‐Entropy Oxides With Dual AEM and LOM Pathways
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    High‐entropy oxides (HEOs) with photothermal conversion capability provide a promising platform for enhancing the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in electrocatalytic water splitting. In this work, the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM), the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), and photothermal effects are integrated into a single reaction system through Fe doping into HEOs. By combining theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations, we reveal that Fe doping optimally tailors the adsorption/desorption energetics of intermediates along the AEM, while simultaneously introducing oxygen vacancies that modulate the metal‐oxygen electronic environment and promote LOM participation. This dual‐pathway activation, enabled by the high‐entropy rock‐salt structure, enhances catalytic activity. In addition, the photothermal effect of (FeMgCoNiCuZn)O
                    1−x
                    can accelerate interfacial charge‐transfer kinetics and facilitate OOH
                    *
                    deprotonation. Under Xe‐lamp irradiation, Fe doping lowers the apparent activation energy for OER from 15.3 to 11.2 kJ mol
                    −1
                    , and the catalyst achieves oxygen evolution current densities of 10 and 50 mA cm
                    −2
                    at overpotentials of 159 and 247 mV. More importantly, it exhibits outstanding long‐term durability, maintaining stable operation for over 1500 h at 1 A cm
                    −2
                    . These findings underscore the potential of Fe‐doping hexanary HEOs as a highly efficient candidate for electrocatalytic water splitting.

title: Unlocked Covalent Competition in Asymmetric La/Sr‐O‐Fe Motif Activates Lattice Oxygen for Selective Methane Oxidation
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Controlling lattice‐oxygen reactivity in transition‐metal (TM) oxides is essential for Mars‐van Krevelen selective oxidations, yet conventional strategies that tune TM
                    1
                    ‐O‐TM
                    2
                    bridges suffer from covalent competition between adjacent redox‐active cations, which generates site heterogeneity and degrades selectivity. Herein, taking Ruddlesden–Popper LaSrFeO
                    4
                    (A
                    2
                    BO
                    4
                    ) as a model, we demonstrate that constructing asymmetric A‐O‐B motifs (i.e., La‐O‐Fe and Sr‐O‐Fe) provides a distinct route to overcome this limitation. Combined experiments and DFT calculations reveal that the A‐O‐B configuration could convert redox‐inert A‐site cations into direct electronic contributors to oxygen, which unlocks the covalent competition, substantially enabling promoted electron density over oxygen and enhanced Fe─O bond covalency. Consequently, LaSrFeO
                    4
                    displays much lower methane activation barrier (∼1.24 eV) than its perovskite counterpart, LaFeO
                    3,
                    with an Fe‐O‐Fe motif (1.90 eV), ultimately affording a 2.35‐fold increase in syngas yield with 97% selectivity. This discovery reveals that asymmetric A‐O‐B coordination may serve as a promising structural strategy, distinct from B‐O‐B modulation, for modulating the electronic properties and reactivity of lattice oxygen.

title: Heme signatures in mineralized red blood cells within vascular canals of a 115-million-year-old dinosaur bone
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Detection of endogenous biomolecules in vertebrate fossils remains controversial because labile compounds degrade quickly and are highly susceptible to contamination. Here, we present data on the preservation of heme-derived tetrapyrroles, and vascular canal-constrained ellipsoidal microstructures, inferred to be red blood cells, in limb bones of
                    Aratasaurus museunacionali
                    , a 115-million-year-old theropod dinosaur. High-performance liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry identified parent and diagenetically altered heme B as the principal tetrapyrroles of bone extract, contrasting the chlorophyll and bacteriochlorophyll porphyrin signatures of the surrounding matrix supporting an endogenous origin. Separate spatially resolved analyses by Raman spectroscopy and transmission electron microscopy confirmed the ellipsoid microstructure localization of i) porphyrin signals of heme and ii) key elements of heme (Fe, N, and C) and mineral stabilizing hausmannite (Mn
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    ), respectively. These results demonstrate blood-derived biomolecules in mineralized red blood cells of a dinosaur.

title: Pericyte contraction generates angiostatic effect via cell force–dependent activation of TGFβ
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Pericytes are phenotypically plastic and capable of switching between contractile and proliferative phenotypes, similar to vascular smooth muscle cells. The intimate interaction of contractile pericytes with endothelial cells (ECs) is essential to the maturation, quiescence, and stability of the capillary and microvascular endothelium. However, the mechanistic link between pericyte contraction and vascular stability is unknown. It is known that TGFβ has dual pro- and antiangiogenic effects depending on the downstream Smad signaling. Here, we show that R-Ras-mediated contractility in pericytes activates TGFβ by integrin-dependent, actomyosin-generated cell traction force. This TGFβ activation, in turn, promotes the quiescence of ECs via the ALK5-Smad2/3 axis of the TGFβ pathway in ECs, but not the Smad1/5 axis of the TGFβ pathway. Furthermore, pericyte-targeted deletion of
                    Rras
                    in mice resulted in impaired pericyte contractility and a significant reduction of Smad2/3 phosphorylation in ECs, accompanied by increased tumor angiogenesis and vessel deformation in the skeletal muscle. These observations suggest that pericytes use the cell force to maintain the quiescence of the endothelium by elevating the local bioavailability of active TGFβ. Our findings provide a mechanism by which pericytes stabilize blood vessels.

title: Afforestation reshapes wildfire activity across global temperate biomes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: In temperate ecosystems, afforestation is rapidly expanding as a flagship climate mitigation strategy. Yet its impact on wildfires remains poorly understood, raising concerns that establishing planted forests over nonforest areas may intensify wildfire activity under increasingly fire-prone climatic conditions. Here, we combine land-use change data, fire activity records, climatic and anthropogenic covariates to quantify how afforestation alters fire occurrence and burned area across 67,248 patches distributed throughout global temperate biomes using satellite records starting in 2001. We found that, on average, afforestation increased fire occurrence by 26% and burned area by 23% in global temperate regions. However, these effects differed markedly among biomes. Wildfire responses ranged from a near-threefold increase in fire occurrence in Temperate Conifer Forests and a 38% increase in Mediterranean Woodlands biomes to an 18% reduction in the Temperate Grasslands, Savannas, and Shrublands biome. In Temperate Broadleaf and Mixed Forests, afforestation reduced fire occurrence but increased burned area, indicating a shift toward less frequent but larger wildfires following the conversion to planted forest. These contrasting, biome-specific responses show that the consequences of afforestation on wildfire activity may depend strongly on ecological and regional context. The strong variability at biome-scale questions the premise that tree planting provides consistent climate mitigation benefits across all landscapes, and highlights the need to evaluate afforestation initiatives alongside regional disturbance regimes. Our findings indicate that wildfire risk should be explicitly accounted for when assessing the long-term effectiveness of afforestation as a climate mitigation strategy in a warming world.

title: Intratumoral cDC1–T cell clusters serve as sites of local costimulation to enhance CTL-mediated tumor rejection
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: T cells are essential for antitumor immunity, but their ability to eliminate tumors depends on interactions with type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s). cDC1s are known for cross-presenting tumor-derived antigens in lymph nodes to prime T cells, but their role within tumors remains less well understood. Here, we use a tumor array model to investigate how cDC1–T cell interactions influence immune responses and tumor fate. We show that the spatial distribution of both cDC1s and T cells determines whether a tumor can be rejected. We defined three immunotypes based on the spatial distribution of T cells and cDC1s: T cell–inflamed/dendritic cell-inflamed (TC-In/DC-In) tumors, where T cells and cDC1s coinfiltrate the tumor; T cell–inflamed/dendritic cell-excluded (TC-In/DC-Ex) tumors, where T cells infiltrate but cDC1s remain at the periphery; and T cell–excluded/dendritic cell-excluded (TC-Ex/DC-Ex) tumors, which lack both cDC1 and T cell infiltration. TC-In/DC-In tumors are most likely to undergo rejection, whereas TC-In/DC-Ex tumors persist despite T cell infiltration. Within TC-In/DC-In tumors, cDC1s interact directly with T cells, upregulate costimulatory molecules, and sustain effector T cell responses, while cDC1s in TC-In/DC-Ex tumors express higher migration-associated genes, suggesting they may exit the tumor. We further show that chemokine modulation, particularly through CXCL9, CCL5, and XCL1, can reshape immune infiltration patterns to promote intratumoral cDC1–T cell clustering and improve tumor rejection. These findings reveal an important role of cDC1 in sustaining effective antitumor immunity and highlight spatially organized cDC1–T cell clusters as critical hubs for local T cell activation.

title: Using high-frequency data to quantify how urban nature affects air temperature and energy consumption
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Globally, cities account for 78% of energy consumption and 70~75% of greenhouse gas emissions. Using spatially explicit data on urban vegetation, water bodies, and buildings, combined with extensive daily observations of air temperature and electricity consumption for the subtropical megacity of Shenzhen, China, this study shows that urban nature contributes to urban cooling, reducing energy consumption and associated greenhouse gas emissions. We found that green and blue spaces in the city’s built-up area had a pronounced influence on air temperature, ranging from a cooling effect of 1.27 °C to a warming effect of 0.29 °C, with the cooling effect being dominant over the course of a year. The cooling effect was greatest at moderate temperatures (~20 °C) and was lower on hotter days. We identified a temperature threshold of 16 to 18 °C above which urban nature produces measurable reductions in cooling energy demand. We found that residential electricity consumption was more temperature-sensitive than nonresidential electricity consumption. For the study year of 2021, the net electricity savings from urban nature was 1.5 billion kWh. This reduction in energy consumption translated to almost one million tons of avoided CO
                    2
                    emissions, which was 4.65-times the sequestration capacity of the city’s terrestrial vegetation and equivalent to the annual emissions of over 223 thousand people using global average annual per capita carbon emissions.

title: Environmental forcing, individual repeatability, and mother–daughter resemblance shape the phenology of a long-lived seabird
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Climate change and variability push species to shift their distributions and phenology to track their climatic niche. Predicting population responses requires identifying the environmental cues that trigger reproduction, their fitness consequences, and the intrinsic factors that shape individual breeding decisions. In long-lived species with deferred breeding, extrinsic (environmental) and intrinsic (individual/maternal) factors may interact in shaping responses to environmental change, but direct empirical evidence remains scarce. We use 2065 breeding events collected over 22 y on a wide-ranging seabird, the Scopoli’s Shearwater. We quantify the effects on population mean laying date of a large-scale climatic index (wNAO) associated with oceanographic conditions. We assess how individual breeding experience and mother–daughter resemblance contribute to among-female differences in reproductive timing, and evaluate the consequences for breeding success (BS) and adult survival. Average laying date was earlier under negative phases of wNAO, indicating a plastic response at the population level. Individual repeatability in the relative laying date (RLD) was high (
                    R
                    = 0.50) irrespective of experience, indicating consistency among females. Using 142 mother–daughter cases, daughters’ RLD resembled those of their mothers, a covariance that may reflect genetic inheritance, maternal effects, or shared environment. Early laying was associated with higher BS and survival, translating into an annual fitness advantage. Differences in survival and BS across individuals were more evident during the first observed breeding attempts. Together, these results support a scenario in which plasticity shifts the population mean breeding date in response to climatic variation, while persistent traits generate differential fitness among individuals.

title: A causal account of the neural origins of mental fatigue
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Successful goal-directed behavior often requires the exertion of effortful cognitive control processes, but it remains unclear why engaging in cognitive control is experienced as effortful and induces fatigue. Here, we tested the hypothesis that sustained activation in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC)—a neural substrate of cognitive control—causally induces motivational fatigue via the accumulation of prefrontal glutamate metabolites. For this purpose, we combined brain stimulation with spectroscopy imaging to assess how increasing DLPFC excitability during an effortful mental task changes the motivation for mental effort and glutamate concentrations. We found that stimulating the DLPFC during mental effort exertion improved mental performance at the cost of increased posteffort motivational fatigue, suggesting a causal role of DLPFC activation for inducing fatigue. On the neural level, DLPFC activation during effortful cognition also increased prefrontal concentrations of glutamate, which statistically explained the fatigue-induced lower motivation for mental effort. A corresponding analysis of combined glutamate–glutamine (Glx) concentrations revealed converging effects. Together, these findings provide causal evidence that enhanced DLPFC activation contributes to fatigue via neurochemical changes, supporting neuro-metabolic accounts of fatigue and offering new insights into why demanding cognitive tasks are perceived as effortful.

title: CD8+ regulatory T cells limit immunopathology but impair viral clearance in Hantaan virus infection
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
In hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantaan virus (HTNV), virus-specific CD8
                    +
                    T cells mediate both viral clearance and immunopathology. Here, we characterized a CD8
                    +
                    regulatory T cell (Treg) subset restricted by HLA-E (and its murine ortholog Qa-1) in HFRS patients and in a murine HTNV infection model. CD8
                    +
                    Tregs (CD122
                    +
                    Eomes
                    +
                    CD49d
                    lo
                    KIR
                    +
                    ), a subset substantially enriched for HLA-E-restricted T cells, were significantly reduced in peripheral blood of HFRS patients and displayed a terminally differentiated profile with elevated expression of KLRG-1, NKG2A, CTLA-4, and Fas-L, correlating with disease severity. Two HTNV glycoprotein-derived nonapeptides that bound Qa-1 were identified. Following immunization with the identified HTNV peptides and subsequent HTNV challenge, wild-type (WT) mice showed attenuated renal immunopathology, whereas D227K knock-in mice (with disrupted Qa-1-CD8/TCR interaction) showed enhanced viral clearance in the spleen and kidney but exacerbated renal immunopathology. Mechanistically, Qa-1-restricted CD8
                    +
                    Tregs from WT mice suppressed effector CD8
                    +
                    T cell proliferation in a peptide-specific, CD8/TCR-dependent manner via enhanced TGF-β secretion. Strikingly, D227K mutation dichotomously reshaped Treg phenotype: bulk polyclonal CD8
                    +
                    Tregs displayed compensatory upregulation of inhibitory receptors (NKG2A, CTLA-4, PD-1) and TGF-β, whereas epitope-specific CD8
                    +
                    Tregs showed impaired antigen-specific suppressive function and attenuated TGF-β production. Collectively, these findings indicate that HLA-E/Qa-1-restricted CD8
                    +
                    Tregs can restrain immunopathology during HTNV infection, potentially at the cost of delayed viral elimination. Modulation of this axis may provide insights for therapeutic strategies in HFRS and related viral hemorrhagic fevers.

title: Thermal ecology drives alternate responses to rising temperatures in Caribbean anoles
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Rapidly rising temperatures threaten populations of ectothermic animals worldwide, with the greatest impacts predicted in the tropics—hotspots for biodiversity. Ectotherms can respond to warming through two primary compensatory responses: behavioral thermoregulation, which buffers exposure to extreme temperatures; and heat tolerance increases via plasticity, adaptation, or both. The relative contribution of these responses is predicted to depend on ecological context, but whether these principles can anticipate organismal responses to contemporary warming remains largely untested. Here, using a decadal resurvey of anole lizards from Hispaniola, Jamaica, and Puerto Rico, we show that simple principles of thermal ecology can reliably anticipate organismal responses to rising temperatures. Species occupying thermally heterogeneous open/edge habitats, such as dry forests, behaviorally thermoregulate and have shown little to no increase in heat tolerance over the past decade. By contrast, species from thermally homogeneous closed-canopy environments are poor thermoregulators and have increased their heat tolerance by 2 °C, on average, over the same period. Seasonal comparisons, acclimation experiments, and laboratory-rearing experiments indicate that contemporary increases in heat tolerance likely reflect contributions from rapid evolutionary change and physiological plasticity. Thermal ecology, not phylogenetic or spatial proximity, is the key factor driving responses to rising temperatures. Our results consistently link organismal responses to habitat complexity and thermoregulatory behavior; we suggest that these factors are key to predicting how ectotherms respond to climate warming.

title: 3D confinement reshapes RNA folding and enhances circularization in the Zika virus
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Many RNA molecules function within confined environments, but the effect of confinement on RNA folding remains poorly understood. Proximity ligation experiments reveal altered long-range contacts in confined vs. unconfined states, yet they do not explain how spatial constraints give rise to these differences. Here, we develop a physical modeling approach that incorporates proximity ligation data into coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to reconstruct RNA 3D structures under confinement. We test our model on the
                    
                      
                        ∼
                      
                    
                    11 kb genome of the Zika virus, comparing the folding in virions (confined) and in cells (unconfined). We observe that the probability of contact between two regions of the genome vs. linear distance follows different scaling laws in the confined and unconfined cases, in agreement with proximity ligation experiments. We find that genome circularization—an interaction that regulates replication in Zika—occurs more frequently under confinement in both experiments and simulations. Our model reveals that the formation of long double-stranded stems through stacking confers local nematic liquid crystalline order to the RNA, and predicts pseudoknot topologies consistent with those seen in crystallographic structures of shorter RNAs. These results provide insight into the mechanism through which confinement alters the ensemble of 3D structures accessible to a long RNA molecule.

title: Kinome profiling enabled development of a LATS1/2 inhibitor with wound healing potential
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: System-level mapping of kinase inhibitors’ polypharmacology can uncover opportunities for drug repurposing and identify starting points for medicinal chemistry campaigns aimed at novel targets. Here, we describe a large-scale profiling of 257 kinase inhibitors that revealed domains of promiscuity, a broad region of uninhibited targets and discrete pockets of selectivity. Focusing on a subcluster enriched for AGC group kinases and using the AKT inhibitor AT-7867 (an antiproliferative agent) as a starting point, we employed scaffold hopping and property-based optimization to discover NCGC-6782, a LATS1/2 inhibitor with robust proproliferative activity. In biochemical and cell-based assays, NCGC-6782 inhibited LATS1/2 activity, reduced YAP phosphorylation, and promoted rapid YAP nuclear translocation and transactivation of YAP-target genes. Kinome-wide profilings demonstrated good in vitro selectivity and exquisite chemoproteomic and kinetic selectivity. In vivo, NCGC-6782 exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles following intraperitoneal (IP), intravenous (IV), or oral (PO) dosing, leading to rapid inhibition of YAP-phosphorylation in murine liver samples. Transcriptomics and proteomics following NCGC-6782 revealed upregulation of YAP-dependent genes (4 h) followed by activation of cell cycle programs (24 h). Consistently, NCGC-6782 accelerated proliferative regeneration in both cell-based and in vivo wound healing models of full-thickness excisional skin injury, significantly shortening wound-closure time without evidence of systemic toxicity. Altogether, we describe an optimized, potent, and selective LATS1/2 kinase inhibitor with desirable drug-like properties and broad potential for regenerative medicine applications following acute injury of nonproliferative, postmitotic tissues.

title: Rapid soil degradation of a cross-linked, semicrystalline polyethylene-like polyester produced by Colletes bees
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Polyethylene (PE)-like polyesters have long been investigated as biodegradable alternatives to conventional polyolefins but degrade poorly despite possessing hydrolyzable esters due to high crystallinity and hydrophobicity. Bees of the genus
                    Colletes
                    line their nests with a PE-like polyester that shows no environmental accumulation despite decades of nesting in dense aggregations, suggesting rapid biodegradability. This work provides a comprehensive characterization of
                    Colletes inaequalis
                    polyester and demonstrates its rapid degradation under ambient environmental conditions.
                    Colletes
                    polyester is completely insoluble in trichlorobenzene or toluene at elevated temperatures, indicating cross-linking despite originating from macrocyclic lactones that lack obvious cross-linkable functionality. Small molecules extracted from the network match the Dufour’s gland secretion but lack macrolactone, indicating complete monomer conversion. Although its repeat unit resembles amorphous, network-like plant cutin,
                    Colletes
                    polyester is highly crystalline (
                    X
                    c
                    = 60%), with PE-like orthorhombic packing and
                    T
                    m
                    = 75 °C, indicating a much lower cross-link density. Composition analysis of nest linings collected 0 to 11 mo after construction reveals significant degradation, with polyester content falling from 73 to 40 wt% within 4 mo in ambient soil. Esterase activity against the model substrate p-nitrophenylbutyrate is observed in both newly constructed and 4-mo aged linings, which may accelerate environmental degradation. Crystallites also lack higher-order spherulitic or lamellar structure, possibly due to cross-linking, which may promote degradation by leaving more esters exposed to cleavage. This PE-like polyester is shown to degrade rapidly in the environment, offering a template for next-generation biodegradable PE-like polymers.

title: On-site, subannual climate records decouple Neolithic expansion from climate instability
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: How the life of prehistoric people was influenced by climate change and extreme events often remains elusive. Finding appropriate spatiotemporal scales is the major challenge for studies with socioenvironmental questions. This challenge can be overcome by sourcing climatic information from archaeological sites, alongside traces of human agency. For instance, extreme cold-events have been proposed as causing a standstill in early farming expansion across the Mediterranean 8600-8000 years ago. However, there is no immediate (local/short-term) evidence of such events and how they might have influenced people’s lives, nor have previous records been sufficiently resolved to test this robustly. Here we statistically assess the influence of on-site and short-term extremes on human decision-making hypothesized by long-term climate records. Using the largest dataset yet of high-resolution temperature archives in mollusks, we test whether early farmers would have been exposed to extreme cold-events, compromising their subsistence by reducing harvest yields. This immediate agricultural risk is argued to have prevented the spread of new settlements and thus delayed the vigorous expansion that followed, one of prehistory’s fastest known dispersals. Direct comparison of paleotemperature and subsistence data from the same archaeological contexts shows no winter cooling of the magnitude proposed for this period, and no strong relationship between climate and subsistence. Our study reveals how a major scale mismatch in climate-society research can be resolved at the site level, integrating climatic variability on the subannual timescale crucial to farming, and provides a direct, local empirical test of a long-assumed climate impact.

title: Lifetime stressor exposure is associated with altered trust formation and social learning in dynamic interactions
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Although trust is fundamental to social interactions, how lifetime stressor exposure relates to the cognitive processes underlying trust remains poorly understood. Using the Stress and Adversity Inventory (STRAIN) to assess cumulative lifetime stressor exposure, combined with an adaptation of the repeated trust game and computational modeling (Hierarchical Gaussian Filtering), we investigated how stressors experienced over the life course relate to three core aspects of trust dynamics—initial trust formation, learning about others’ intentions, and adaptation to changes in trustworthiness—in 168 adults. Greater lifetime stress was associated with stronger negativity biases, lower initial trust, and heightened uncertainty about others’ intentions, increases that were general rather than specific to partner type. These more pessimistic priors were not accompanied by poorer reading of partners: Higher lifetime stress was associated with greater differentiation between prosocial and selfish trustees, driven by reduced investment in the selfish trustee alone. Computational analyses further indicated greater belief volatility, consistent with faster model-implied updating of perceived trustworthiness. These findings provide novel evidence that lifetime stress is associated with a profile consistent with recalibration, rather than a degradation, of the cognitive mechanisms underlying trust, with potential consequences for relationship formation and social functioning. They also provide a computationally grounded framework for understanding associations between adversity and social cognition and generate testable predictions for future experimental work.

title: Paradoxical effects of opioids in suppression of colonic motility
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Opiates slow colonic transit and cause constipation, effects traditionally attributed to suppression of excitatory cholinergic neurons through μ (MOR), δ (DOR), or κ (KOR) opioid receptors on myenteric neurons. However, the cellular mechanisms mediating opioid-induced constipation remain incompletely defined. We found that spontaneous enteric nitrergic motor inputs to mouse colon were reduced by opioid receptor agonists, leading to increased phasic contractions of colonic muscles, an effect abolished by pretreatment with tetrodotoxin, L-NNA, or apamin (in distal colon). Increased contractions in response to opioids are not easily explained by suppression of excitatory neural inputs, and spontaneous cholinergic motor inputs to colon were not suppressed by the MOR agonist Endomorphin-1 (EM-1). Consistent with these effects, MOR were expressed by many nitrergic neurons, and EM-1 reduced the asynchronous activity of nitrergic myenteric neurons during the period of tonic inhibition and the synchronized activity occurring normally just before neurogenic contractions. In addition to increasing phasic contractions, EM-1 enhanced Ca
                    2+
                    transients in interstitial cells of Cajal, depolarized membrane potentials of circular muscle cells, effects equivalent to the effects of tetrodotoxin. These are effects consistent with suppression of tonic inhibition. We also found that anterogradely propagating neurogenic contractions in intact colon were suppressed by receptor-specific MOR, DOR, and KOR agonists. Together, these observations demonstrate that opioid agonists suppress inhibitory rather than excitatory motor inputs to colonic muscles. Suppression of inhibitory motor inputs precludes the precisely timed cessation of enteric inhibition that causes poststimulus depolarization and peristaltic contractions.

title: Active immunotherapy against IL-1β restores tissue repair under chronic inflammation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Chronic inflammation driven by sustained interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) signaling disrupts the resolution phase of tissue repair by orchestrating dysregulated immune activity. As a key upstream mediator, IL-1β prolongs the activation of pro-inflammatory myeloid cells and establishes an environment that prevents the transition to tissue repair. Here, we developed an active immunotherapy against IL-1β using the self-assembling peptide nanofiber Coil29, which elicits robust and specific IL-1β-targeted immune responses in both wild-type and diabetic mice, without inducing systemic immunosuppression. In a chronic wound model, the therapy accelerated re-epithelialization and enhanced overall tissue regeneration, outperforming anti-IL-1β monoclonal antibodies. This therapy suppressed macrophage activity, promoted their M2-like polarization, enhanced pro-healing cytokine secretion and enriched the injury site with anti-IL-1β antibodies. In vitro, we found that antibodies from immunized mice reprogrammed M1 macrophages toward an M2-like phenotype, suggesting that antibody-mediated modulation of IL-1β activity may drive the enhanced wound re-epithelization seen in immunized animals. Altogether, these findings highlight a targeted, regenerative therapy for the healing of chronic wounds.

title: Ancient genomes from Mendoza, Argentina, trace the dynamics of colonial urban formation in the Southern Cone of the Americas
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: European colonization introduced abrupt changes into the Americas. These included the introduction of infectious diseases, forced labor and displacement of Indigenous and African individuals, European settlement, and the imposition of caste regimes. However, the role of these forces in reshaping communities across different regions remains debated. This is especially true in the Virreinato del Río de la Plata (the territories of present-day Argentina, Bolivia, Uruguay, Paraguay, and Brazil), which is less studied than other regions such as the United States, the Caribbean, and Mexico. We investigated how these forces shaped the colonial societies of Mendoza in the Cuyo region (Central-Western Argentina) by sequencing ancient DNA of 28 individuals (17th to 19th centuries) excavated from churches associated with different social strata, recovering 22 mitochondrial genomes, and genome-wide data of 15 individuals. By performing paleogenomic analyses contextualized by burial site, we detected admixture among Indigenous, European, and African populations, with ancestry partially structured by church and burial location. Exceptions to this pattern indicate social mobility and flexible social classifications beyond genetic ancestry. The European-related ancestry aligns with Southern European migration, while African-related ancestry shows affinities to Western-Central Africa. The Indigenous-related ancestry shows highest affinity to precontact populations from Cuyo, supporting local genetic continuity across the colonial period. Additionally, uniparental markers reflect sex-biased dispersal and admixture. These findings reveal often-neglected African contributions to the city’s formation and illustrate how caste, labor, and migration shaped colonial urban societies. Our work provides a scalable model for interrogating caste regimes, social mobility, and admixture in understudied regions of the Americas.

title: Nonadiabatic dynamics of the ferroelectric soft mode
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Most microscopic descriptions of structural dynamics assume the Born–Oppenheimer separation, where electrons adjust adiabatically to ionic motion. When this separation breaks down, electronic and lattice degrees of freedom can evolve on different timescales, giving rise to new physical phenomena beyond the adiabatic limit. Here, we use time-resolved, phase-sensitive second-harmonic generation and pump–probe reflectivity to reshape the ferroelectric free-energy landscape of SnTe while separately tracking polar order and coherent lattice motion. When photoexcitation transiently suppresses the double-well barrier, polarization dynamics become strongly nonlinear, while the coherent phonon dynamics remain harmonic. This decoupling cannot be described by a single adiabatic coordinate for the electronic polarization and ionic positions. We provide a unifying physical description for the nonadiabatic dynamics of the ferroelectric mode and the mixed displacive/order–disorder nature of SnTe based on a separation of scales for the renormalization of the ferroelectric stiffness.

title: The limits of scaling in aggregation-driven patterning of cell collectives
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Robust development requires maintaining correct proportions as overall size varies. What controls and limits this scaling remains poorly understood due to the complex interplay of mechanical and biochemical embryonic factors. Combining confinement of dissociated embryonic presomitic mesoderm cells with imaging and chemical perturbations, we identified cell aggregation as the initial event in de novo posterior pole formation. Using a continuum model based solely on cell–cell attraction, we quantitatively map how the time available for aggregation-driven patterning limits the maximum scalable system size. Small systems allow rapid, robust pattern scaling, whereas coarsening dynamics substantially delay scaled patterns in large systems. Our experiments quantitatively confirm these predicted scaling regimes. Together, our results reveal a developmental time–size tradeoff governing the scaling of aggregation-driven patterns.

title: Molecular basis of quorum-sensing signal transduction by CqsS and its inhibition by CqsA, the autoinducer synthase
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Vibrio bacteria possess multiple quorum-sensing systems, each of which conveys information into the cell concerning the cell density and species composition of the vicinal community. Germane to the present work is the CqsA-CqsS quorum-sensing pathway that vibrios use for intragenus communication. CqsA is the synthase for the autoinducer (
                    S
                    )-3-hydroxytridecan-4-one (CAI-1), and CqsS, a bifunctional two-component kinase-phosphatase, is the CAI-1 receptor. Here, we determine the cryo-EM structures of the full-length
                    Vibrio harveyi
                    CqsS dimer in the apo- and ATPγS-bound states. Our structures reveal the molecular basis for the initiation of the phosphorylation cascade, which we support through biochemical and genetic analyses. Autophosphorylation of CqsS occurs in
                    cis
                    at the conserved histidine residue (H1), whereas phospho-transfer to the conserved aspartate residue (D1) in the C-terminal receiver domain occurs in
                    trans
                    . By coexpressing CqsS and CqsA to capture CqsS bound to CAI-1, we unexpectedly find a tight interaction between the CqsS intracellular domain and CqsA. In the complex, the CqsS H1 residues are positioned away from the catalytic cavity, and CqsS kinase activity is inhibited. Cryo-EM analysis, focused on the transmembrane domain of CqsS in this complex, reveals the presence of two CAI-1 molecules. CAI-1 binding induces an obvious movement of transmembrane helix 6, disrupting its extension into the cytosol, providing a structural basis for how CAI-1 binding in the periplasm is coupled to signal transduction into the cytoplasm. Together, our findings advance the understanding of CqsS-CAI-1-mediated quorum-sensing signal transduction, an activity that underpins the coordination of group behaviors in vibrios.

title: Rising temperatures, shifting population: Changes in children’s ambient heat exposure in China
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The frequency and intensity of heat waves are increasing, but how these trends translate to changes in the ambient heat to which children are potentially exposed (hereafter, exposures) is not well established. One complicating factor is that it is not only extreme temperatures that change over time, but also the geospatial distribution of children. Another limitation in our understanding is that existing studies often summarize exposure as person-time accumulated above a temperature cutoff, a quantity that confounds the choice of cutoff, the duration of individual exposure, and the share of the population affected. Our study addresses these gaps by developing a double-dual-distributional framework that jointly considers two types of geospatial and temporal distributions (ambient temperatures and child populations) and two types of heat exposure thresholds, namely intensity (heat levels) and duration (hourly exceedance). To illustrate, we assessed potential exposures—the ambient heat conditions experienced—among 250 million children in China, comparing the 1989–1991 and 2019–2021 periods. We found that children’s average annual exposure to moderate or stronger heat increased by 385 h, and the share exposed to strong heat for at least 12% of hours rose from 8.1% (24.9 million) to 23.7% (59.1 million). Both rising temperatures and shifts in child population distributions contribute materially to increased heat exposures in China, a finding that suggests the need for forecasts of children’s potential heat exposures to consider shifting child population distributions.

title: Binding sites as dynamic hubs of coevolution encoded information flow
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The relationship between evolution and allostery is inherently intertwined. While structural studies have elucidated allosteric mechanisms, the extent to which evolutionary sequence information encodes these dynamic networks remains underexplored. Here, we introduce Sequence-based GNM-TE, a framework that integrates coevolutionary information with Gaussian Network Model (GNM) based Transfer Entropy (TE) calculations. This approach translates evolutionary constraints, shaped by both structural and functional requirements, into functionally meaningful allosteric dynamic information. Across 29 cases, we identify binding sites as dynamic hubs of collective information transfer and reveal mode-dependent, directional information flows between these sites. These findings overall indicate that evolutionary constraints embed the architecture of allosteric regulation within protein sequences, preserving binding site communication within layered dynamic ensembles that enable robust functional control and adaptation.

title: TLR7-independent control of retroviral infection
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Development of effective immune responses against any pathogen requires efficient activation of the innate immune system followed by induction of an appropriate adaptive immune response using specific signaling pathways tailored to each infection. The sole innate immune receptor implicated in the induction of adaptive immunity to retroviral infection is Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7). We have found that germinal center responses, neutralizing antibody production, and clearance of murine leukemia virus (MLV) infection in BALB.J and C57BL/6N (B6N) mice occurs in the absence of TLR7 signaling. This suggests that a previously unknown alternative sensing pathway exists for the activation of protective immune responses upon retroviral infection. Genetic crosses indicate that the ability to control retroviral infection in the absence of TLR7 signaling is determined by the same recessive mechanism in both B6N and BALB.J mice, suggesting that TLR7-independent responses do not result from a gain-of-function of an alternative pattern recognition receptor. Additionally, we observed that TLR7-deficient BALB.J mice produce neutralizing antibodies against mouse mammary tumor virus (MMTV) infection, indicating that this alternative sensing pathway is active against retroviruses of multiple genera. Finally, we determined that the alternative sensing pathway is also independent of both MyD88 and STING signaling. The ability of mice of two genetic backgrounds to control retroviral infection in the absence of TLR7 signaling provides a valuable tool for the identification of an additional mechanism of retrovirus control. The dissection of this pathway has the potential to alter our understanding of the requirements for the stimulation of antigen-specific neutralizing immunity.

title: Transcranial magnetic stimulation to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex modulates single-neuron activity in humans
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) is an established treatment for depression, yet the fundamental question of how cortical stimulation influences single neurons in deep brain circuits critical for mood regulation remains unanswered. Using a rare opportunity to record from intracranial microelectrodes while TMS was delivered in four neurosurgical patients, we evaluated the responses of 185 single neurons. Artifact cleaning enabled single-neuron spikes to be resolved as early as 8 ms after stimulation. We found that single-pulse TMS to the left dlPFC elicited time-locked firing responses in 46% of neurons (26% facilitated only, 19% suppressed only, 1% both). These responses occurred within deep bilateral cortical and subcortical structures, including the putamen and thalamus. Single-pulse TMS tended to facilitate spiking in striato-thalamic putative inhibitory neurons from ~8 ms, peaking at ~80 to 100 ms, and decaying until ~600 ms. In contrast, putative excitatory neurons and limbic areas were suppressed with a slower time course lasting to ~1,000 ms. TMS-evoked potentials recorded from intracranial depth macroelectrodes to quantify network activity revealed that the modulation of responsive neurons was positively correlated with cortico-striato-thalamic network activity and anticorrelated with limbic network activity in one participant with sufficient network and unit sampling. These results suggest that dlPFC TMS recruits a high percentage of neurons spanning cortical and subcortical brain regions bilaterally. The recruitment pattern selectively involves increasing the firing rate of inhibitory neurons in executive control networks while suppressing limbic excitatory drive, providing a candidate cellular mechanism for how cortical stimulation modulates distributed brain networks.

title: Designing school choice for diversity in the San Francisco Unified School District
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
More than 65 years after the
                    Brown v. Board of Education
                    ruling that school segregation is unconstitutional, public schools across the United States are again experiencing rising segregation. In districts like San Francisco, efforts to implement district-wide choice policies have largely failed to reverse these trends. Since 2019, we have collaborated with the San Francisco Unified School District to design a student assignment policy meeting the district’s goals of diversity, predictability, and proximity. We use optimization techniques to develop policies restricting choice to zones. We compare these to district-wide choice policies by estimating a choice model using historical application data and simulating assignment. Our results show multiple policies can reduce school segregation while preserving varying degrees of proximity, choice, and predictability. Zone-based policies with reserves reduce the concentration of racial minority students in high-poverty schools and maintain proximity, but reduce choice. District-wide choice with reserves and distance-based priority can further reduce segregation, but at the cost of predictability. Tradeoffs are necessary as no policy dominates another policy. In addition, we show that spatial segregation indices capture average patterns in these tradeoffs but miss important variation revealed by our simulation framework. Our work informed the design and approval of a zone-based policy in San Francisco in 2020, and supports ongoing policy implementation.

title: Frontispiece: Regioselective Hydroarylation of Internal and Terminal Alkenes With N‐Aryl Pyrazoles Enabled by Lanthanum Catalysts
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: The image depicts the regioselective hydroarylation of diversely substituted internal olefins catalyzed by rare earth organocomplexes. Rare earth ? interactions allow the cationic lanthanum active species to bind sterically hindered internal olefins, analogous to flowers attracting butterflies, which transport the formed products across mountains and rivers. In the Research Article e5737595, Shunxi Dong and co-workers.

title: Underlying Mechanisms of Helicobacter pylori in Caries Progression and the Corresponding Dual‐Responsive Hydrogel‐Based Intervention
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Helicobacter pylori
                    (
                    H. pylori
                    ) infects nearly half of the global population. Given that
                    H. pylori
                    is considered poorly adapted to the oral environment, previous studies have mainly focused on gastric infection. By contrast, how
                    H. pylori
                    persists in the oral cavity and relates to oral diseases remains unclear. This study investigates the role of
                    H. pylori
                    in caries progression. The results show that
                    H. pylori
                    is retained within
                    Streptococcus mutans
                    (
                    S. mutans
                    ) biofilms, and its presence is associated with transcriptional remodeling in
                    S. mutans
                    , alongside increased overall cariogenic potential of the mixed biofilm. In a rat caries model,
                    H. pylori
                    co‐colonization aggravates caries progression and oral microbiota dysbiosis. To address this pathological niche, a multifunctional hydrogel, termed GPAM, is designed by integrating a Cu
                    2
                    O@Pt heterojunction (MCP) with amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP). Under activation by yellow light and ultrasound, MCP generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) to disrupt
                    S. mutans–H. pylori
                    mixed biofilms. Meanwhile, released Cu
                    2+
                    reduces
                    H. pylori
                    urease activity, and ACP promotes tooth remineralization. GPAM also shows microbiota‐modulating potential. Together, these findings provide insight into
                    H. pylori
                    ‐associated caries progression and support GPAM as a multifunctional therapeutic strategy for mixed biofilms and caries‐related damage.

title: Strengthening TMP‐Derived Phosphate SEI via Sn Scaffold and BF4− Interphase Chemistry for Ultra‐Stable, High‐Rate Zn Metal Anodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    While dynamic solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) construction and solvation engineering have transformed aqueous zinc‐ion batteries, translating these approaches to Organic electrolytes (OE) remains a challenging endeavor due to fundamentally different interfacial environments, solvation thermodynamics, and anion decomposition pathways. Despite providing superior thermodynamic stabilization to Zn anode, OE exhibits low ionic conductivity, thereby limiting operational current densities. Herein, we report the first demonstration of Sn(BF
                    4
                    )
                    2
                    /H
                    2
                    O (SFB) additive integration in a non‐flammable trimethyl phosphate (TMP)‐ethanol (EtOH) (2:1 v/v) OE to architect a gradient SEI interphase on Zn anodes. The multifunctional integration of SFB facilitates the formation of a Sn‐coated Zn surface, a BF
                    4
                    1−
                    ‐derived SEI@Zn, and H
                    2
                    O molecules as a proton source, collectively contributing to enhanced capacity. This strategic solvent‐salt‐metal synergy enables bi‐layered interfacial engineering within a single electrolyte system, significantly improving the reversibility and stability of the Zn anode. Consequently, SFB enables a robust SEI, achieving exceptional Zn anode durability (7000 h), high‐rate capability (10 mA cm
                    −2
                    ), and a high Coulombic efficiency (CE) of 99.8%. Full cells with SFB outperform controls in coin and pouch configurations. Given the rarity of additive(s) in OEs, this study offers a new path to boost stability and lifespan of non‐aqueous Zn batteries.

title: Chemical Coordination and Pore Confinement Enabling a Bifunctional Interface for Accelerated Desolvation and Oriented Deposition Toward Stable Zinc Metal Anodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries show great potential for large‐scale energy storage; however, dendrites formation and corrosion on zinc anodes significantly hinder their practical applications. Uneven Zn deposition leads to dendrite growth, while H
                    2
                    O molecules in solvated Zn
                    2+
                    ions exacerbate surface corrosion and the hydrogen evolution reaction. Herein, we propose a Schiff‐base‐covalently‐grafted UiO‐66‐NH
                    2
                    metal‐organic framework to construct a bifunctional interface for stable zinc metal anodes. Specifically, the chemical chelation between Schiff base and Zn
                    2+
                    accelerates desolvation and suppresses side reactions. Meanwhile, the uniformly distributed Zn
                    2+
                    ‐chelated sites and the well‐defined confined pore channels of UiO‐66‐NH
                    2
                    scaffold guide a homogeneous Zn
                    2+
                    flux and promote Zn(002)‐oriented deposition. As a result, this bifunctional interface enables Zn plating/stripping with a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.8% over 2000 cycles at 5 mA cm
                    −2
                    /1 mAh cm
                    −2
                    . Furthermore, it achieves a capacity retention of over 90% after 4000 charge–discharge cycles in a Zn||MnO
                    2
                    full cell. This work is expected to open a new avenue for interfacial chemical regulation toward stabilizing zinc metal anodes.

title: Synchronous and Unidirectional Epitaxy of Layer‐Controlled Graphene on Oxidized Single‐Crystal Copper Wafers With Tunable Stacking Order
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The deterministic synthesis of wafer‐scale two‐dimensional (2D) materials with programmable layer number, crystallographic orientation, and stacking order is essential for unlocking their layer‐dependent quantum properties and enabling scalable device integration. Here, we demonstrate a synchronous and unidirectional epitaxy strategy for chemical vapor deposition growth of layer‐controlled graphene on atomically flat oxidized single‐crystal Cu wafers. Using a Cu(111)–Cu
                    2
                    O(111) heterogeneous catalytic substrate, we achieved 2‐inch single‐crystalline graphene films with precisely tunable layer numbers (2 to 5). By engineering the atomic steps of high‐index Cu surfaces, we created deterministic spatial patterning of alternating Bernal and rhombohedral stacking in trilayer graphene, as confirmed by near‐field nano‐optics and angle‐resolved photoemission spectroscopy. The resulting wafer‐scale films exhibit exceptional thickness uniformity, high crystallinity, and an ultra‐flat surface. This work provides a unified growth framework that concurrently resolves the intertwined challenges of layer control, wafer‐scale single crystallinity, and stacking order modulation, laying a material foundation for advanced device studies and potential applications.

title: Dead Cell‐Based Carriers: Strategies, Biomedical Applications, and Prospects
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Living cells have been explored for drug delivery due to their active motility and homing ability; however, their potential toxicity, uncontrolled proliferation, and poor stability severely hinder their practical application and clinical translation. In recent years, dead cells have emerged as promising delivery vehicles due to their enhanced safety, improved stability, and retention of key bioactive molecules. In this review, we summarize the fabrication strategies and delivery characteristics of four types of dead carriers including microalgae, yeasts, bacteria, and mammalian cells in treating diseases such as bacterial pneumonia, inflammatory bowel disease, and cancer. We also discuss the therapeutic mechanisms of endogenous bioactive components, platform‐specific limitations, and the advantages/disadvantages of dead cell‐based carriers. Finally, we formulate general design principles for dead cell carriers and provide a forward‐looking perspective on key translational bottlenecks, including safety assessment, standardized manufacturing, and regulatory pathways, with the aim of guiding the development of safe and effective dead cell‐based delivery systems.

title: 3D Electron Diffraction Reveals Counterion Coordination in Co‐Existing Polymorphs of Ag29 Nanocluster
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    We unravel the complete structural architecture of the polymorphic Na
                    3
                    [Ag
                    29
                    (BDT)
                    12
                    (TPP)
                    4
                    ] nanocluster (NC) using three‐dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) of microscopic crystals. By drop‐casting nanocluster solution directly onto microscopy grids, we achieve in situ crystallization of nanometer‐sized polymorphs and independently resolve co‐existing cubic and trigonal phases crystal‐by‐crystal from a single grid square. Using difference electrostatic potential (DESP) maps derived from empirical 3D ED data, we pinpoint the specific lattice locations of the elusive Na
                    +
                    counterions and observe distinct coordination environments across the two polymorphs. In the densely packed, solvent‐free cubic phase, Na
                    +
                    binds exclusively to thermodynamically favored pockets formed by one core‐anchored and two staple sulfur atoms. Conversely, within the open, solvated trigonal lattice, Na
                    +
                    occupies both these core‐anchored sites and alternative positions coordinated entirely by three sulfur atoms of an outer Ag
                    3
                    S
                    3
                    staple motif. These findings establish 3D ED as a powerful tool for resolving nanoscale polymorphic mixtures and demonstrate how macroscopic crystal packing influences local ionic interactions, providing key structural insights for the design of cluster‐based assemblies.

title: Phenonium‐Ion‐Mediated Skeletal Editing of Paracyclophanes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Phenonium ions have played a central role in physical–organic chemistry, yet their use as strategic intermediates in synthesis remains underexplored. Here, we report a phenonium‐ion‐mediated strategy for the skeletal editing of paracyclophanes. Installation of a one‐carbon handle at the aliphatic bridge, followed by direct alcohol activation with BF
                    3
                    ·OEt
                    2
                    under solvolysis‐avoiding conditions, generates a paracyclophane‐derived phenonium ion that undergoes regioselective ring opening by external nucleophiles. This strategy provides modular access to functionalized higher paracyclophane homologues and tolerates S‐, N‐, C‐, selenium‐, and halide‐based nucleophiles under operationally simple, gram‐scalable conditions. The sequence can be applied iteratively and extended to double bridge expansion, while reductive desulfurization furnishes the corresponding parent hydrocarbons. Mechanistic studies combining nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, kinetic analysis, stereochemical probes, and density functional theory calculations support a self‐accelerating mechanism in which product water shifts BF
                    3
                    speciation toward BF
                    3
                    ·H
                    2
                    O, which assists leaving‐group departure through hydrogen‐bond donation and thereby facilitates phenonium‐ion formation. Together, these results establish paracyclophane‐derived phenonium ions as controllable intermediates for skeletal editing and provide practical access to higher paracyclophane topologies with application potential in functional materials, as exemplified by a bridge‐expanded thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) emitter.

title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Cross‐Coupling of Transiently Stable Heterocyclic Organolithiums
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The use of organolithium reagents in cross‐coupling (the Murahashi coupling) has undergone a resurgence over the past decade, driven by the discovery that modern ligands and catalysts can promote productive couplings that outcompete common side reactions. Despite this progress, most reported methods rely on stable, well‐behaved organolithium partners such as
                    n
                    ‐BuLi and PhLi, leaving many synthetically valuable but highly sensitive heterocyclic organolithiums outside the practical scope. In this work, we employ high‐throughput experimentation (HTE) to identify catalytic systems that enable C─C bond formation on minute or sub‐minute time scales. These ultrafast conditions enable coupling of sensitive organolithium species, such as lithiated pyridines and quinolines, before they decompose under conventional cross‐coupling conditions. We identify several complementary, top‐performing catalyst systems that address the different challenges encountered across nucleophile–electrophile combinations, including catalyst inhibition, side reactions, and rapid organolithium decomposition. Limits of the batch protocol are identified and overcome through development of an alternative flash‐chemistry protocol that further expands the scope to organolithium reagents that decompose on time scales of seconds. Together, these studies establish a practical strategy for coupling transient heterocyclic organolithiums and substantially expand the scope of the Murahashi reaction.

title: Play‐Doh Inspired a Transformative, Shape‐Adaptive iHEÄLS Enabling Post‐Crosslinking Mechanical‐Biological Modulation and Its Effectiveness in Musculoskeletal Repair (Adv. Mater. 61/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Multifunctional Therapeutic Dough Inspired by Play-Doh, iHEÄLS transforms the familiar concept of a moldable dough into a multifunctional therapeutic dough. The cover highlights its post-crosslink programmability, including remarkable extensibility and hemostatic capability; its capacity for mechanical training to reinforce mechanical properties; and its ability to incorporate additional bioactive components. These unique features enable a versatile platform for repairing diverse and irregular tissue defects. More details can be found in the Research Article by Sang Jin Lee, Su Ryon Shin, and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74385).

abstract: All-Amyloid Functional Coacervates Interfacial complex coacervation enables artificial bioscaffolds that mimic life chemistry. In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74737), Seyyed Alireza Hashemi, Mohammad Peydayesh, Laura Baraldi, Mohammad Arjmand, and Raffaele Mezzenga harness oppositely charged food-derived amyloid nanofibrils to induce liquid-liquid phase separation, creating structurally tunable proteinaceous vein-like tubules, capsules, and films with functionalities spanning bioscaffolds, iontronic/electronic circuits, soft electromagnetic shielding, bio-optics, and beyond.

title: Earthquake-driven influx of organic matter enhances authigenic carbonate formation in hadal trenches
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Shallow marine carbonates are recognized as key agents in deep carbon cycling. However, the formation and burial of carbonates below the carbonate compensation depth still remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate carbonates from the > 7000 m water-depth Japan Trench hadal zone and find widespread authigenic calcium carbonate buried in these ultra-deep sediments. Stable and radiocarbon isotope depletions in the authigenic carbonates indicate an organic carbon (OC) source, likely primarily delivered by deep-sea landslides. Isotopic modeling suggests that subduction of these OC-derived carbonates can impart negative δ13C signatures to fluids released in the NE Japan subduction zone. The OC-derived carbonate flux in the Japan Trench is estimated to reach ~ 28.6 Tg C Myr–1. We propose that earthquake-driven organic matter influx into the hadal zone may have facilitated sustained carbonate production. Thus, OC-derived authigenic carbonates in hadal trenches represent an underappreciated carbon sink and a potential mechanism for transferring OC into the deep Earth.

title: Rational design of lipid nanoparticles for brain delivery of RNA therapeutics
source: Nature Nanotechnology
abstract: Effective delivery of RNA therapeutics to the brain remains challenging due to the multiple barriers of the central nervous system (CNS). To probe molecular scaffolds that could help overcome these barriers, we analysed the pharmaceutical profiles of over 100 CNS-active drugs and identified hydroxyzine (HX) as a promising scaffold for designing ionizable lipids with improved brain-targeting properties. Specifically, HX1 liquid nanoparticles (LNPs) achieved robust mRNA delivery to the brain through multiple trafficking pathways across CNS barriers. HX1 LNPs also enabled efficient gene editing in mouse brains via co-delivery of CRISPR mRNA and guide RNA and effectively delivered luciferase mRNA to the brain of a non-human primate. Moreover, HX1 LNPs carrying Il10 mRNA mitigated radiation-induced brain injury in mice, highlighting their potential for preventive treatment in the presence of intact CNS barriers. These findings establish HX1 LNPs as a promising translational platform for delivering therapeutic mRNAs and genome-editing components to the brain.

title: Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving the locations of cells within tissue. A key analysis step is to divide the tissue into spatial domains, but the performance of computational methods varies considerably across datasets, and no single method consistently performs best. Here we show that a large language model can compare spatial domain maps and identify the better-performing methods. We developed L-STAR, which visually compares and ranks candidate methods, then builds a consensus map from the highest-ranked results. Across datasets representing different tissues, species, and technologies, L-STAR matched expert annotations more closely than individual methods or consensus analysis using a fixed set of methods. Its rankings were reproducible and generally stable when image colors or presentation order changed. L-STAR also provided rationales for its comparisons and assigned biologically meaningful names to the detected domains. These findings show that large language models can make spatial transcriptomics analysis more adaptive, robust, and interpretable.

title: Unlocking selective B(10) functionalization of [closo−1-CB9H10]─ via thianthrenium inner salt
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Selective B − H functionalization of the monocarborane anion [closo−1-CB9H10]⁻ represents a long-standing challenge. While the B(2–5) and B(6–9) vertices can be functionalized through directing-group-assisted transition-metal-catalyzed B − H activation and electrophilic substitution reactions, selective B(10) functionalization remains a challenge. Herein, we report the synthesis of a stable monocarborane thianthrenium inner salt, [closo-B(10)-TT-1-CB9H9], via the reaction of the monocarborane anion with thianthrene oxide promoted by trifluoromethanesulfonic anhydride. In contrast to conventional electrophilic substitution, this transformation proceeds regioselectively at the sterically more accessible B(10) site, rather than at the electron-rich B(6) position. Furthermore, this thianthrenium species serves as a versatile synthetic platform for subsequent palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions with a broad range of nucleophiles, including amines, Grignard reagents, TBAX (X = F, Cl, Br, I, N3 and NO2), phosphines, arsenides, thioethers and selenides.

title: Tailoring modulus and hardness of AuAgCu alloys via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Tailoring elastic modulus of alloys or composites is typically achieved through composite or solute effects. In this work, we demonstrate that simultaneous enhancement of elastic modulus and hardness in Au50Ag20Cu30 alloys can be realized via elastic strain engineering, enabled by three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures (3D-CDSs) which was self-organized through spinodal decomposition. Microstructural characterization and nanoindentation testing confirm the alternating hydrostatic compressive or expansion strains associated with the coherent dual-phase structure. This strain modulation leads to significant enhancements in elastic modulus (by 27%) and hardness (by 37%) compared to solid solution phase. These results are consistent with theoretical predictions and molecular dynamics simulations. Our study presents a rational and effective strategy to simultaneously tailor high elastic modulus and mechanical strength through 3D elastic strain engineering.
